column2: A vast underground customs hall built inside a Victorian brick sewer chamber directly below a Manhattan manhole: high above, the round manhole opening glows with dawn light and a shaft of light falls through steam onto the hall; far down the hall a row of tiny customs booths made from upturned tin cans and matchboxes with little lamps, a giant dropped leather suitcase as big as a building lying open as a baggage carousel, brass rubber stamps the size of barrels, queues of brown sewer rats with tiny luggage waiting at the booths far away, wet cobbled brick floor reflecting the light.

A gigantic subway station staircase seen from the bottom step at the eye level of a rat: worn concrete steps each as tall as a wall rising into the light of a New York subway mezzanine, green painted steel railings, a colossal triangle of pepperoni pizza lying on the stairs halfway up like a fallen monument with melted cheese dripping over a step edge, votive candles in bottle caps and tiny paper offerings left by rats along the bottom step, a hand painted shrine sign, white tiled walls, fluorescent light.

An endless underground hall of illuminated water treatment settling tanks converted into a goldfish aquarium city: huge glass walled tanks glowing aqua and teal stretching into the distance, thousands of orange goldfish swimming in them, painted fake countryside murals of farms and a red barn on the tank walls, a tiny goldfish real estate office with a sign that says UPSTATE, a giant porcelain toilet bowl rim arching over the far end like a gate, wet concrete floor with puddles reflecting the cyan light.

A dim velvet lounge built inside an old round brick sewer tunnel: snowmelt trickling down the far end of the tunnel in a shaft of cold winter light, a small stage with a red curtain, a vintage microphone, tiny round cocktail tables made from bottle caps with candle stubs, framed yellowed newspaper clippings hanging on the curved brick walls, a huge empty leather armchair facing the stage, warm amber lamps and cigarette haze, a green neon sign that says NEW YORKERS.

A towering gothic cathedral nave carved out of a colossal fatberg of congealed grease beneath the city: translucent amber and ivory waxy walls lit from behind like alabaster, pillars of solidified fat with embedded wet wipes, plastic forks and butter wrappers like fossils, a rose window made of a giant takeout container lid glowing gold, an altar made from a melted candle the size of a house, rows of bottle cap pews, warm candlelight.

A trading floor at rat scale under a New York bakery: a canyon of giant conveyor belts and flour sacks receding into the distance, a colossal everything bagel and a croissant the size of houses on the belts, a huge glowing green and red split flap price board high on the far wall listing CRUMB, SESAME, RYE, SCHMEAR with numbers, rats in tiny loosened ties shouting with paper slips far away, a giant calculator and a pocket watch as furniture, warm flour dust in the light.

Looking up and across a lost property depot under a sidewalk subway grate: bright daylight slicing down through the steel grate high above with silhouettes of passing shoes, below it mountains of lost things at colossal scale: white wireless earbuds as big as boulders, yellow transit cards as big as doors, brass keys, a wedding ring like a monument, coins, a lipstick, sunglasses, a single glove, all neatly tagged with paper claim tickets on string, metal shelving canyons, wet concrete floor.

A secret Victorian pneumatic subway tunnel: a perfectly round brick tunnel receding into darkness, an ornate cylindrical carriage upholstered in red velvet with brass trim waiting on the track, gas lamps with frosted globes, a grand painted departure board with gold lettering, a giant fan housing like a ship engine at the far end, frescoed panels, a goldfish bowl on a pedestal, a grand piano, everything slightly dusty and magnificent, warm gaslight.

A luxury spa built among sweating giant steam pipes under the city: huge insulated pipes and brass valve wheels as big as Ferris wheels, plumes of white steam glowing in pink and teal light, tiled plunge pools made from soup cans and sardine tins full of steaming water, tiny folded white towels, rats wrapped in towels lounging on bottle cap loungers far away, eucalyptus in a teacup, a hand lettered sign that says MLOW SPA, condensation dripping.

The abandoned 1904 City Hall subway station at rat scale: a sweeping curved platform under elegant vaulted ceilings of cream and green Guastavino tile, leaded glass skylights pouring soft daylight, brass chandeliers, the curved track bed beside the platform, on the platform far away a tiny rat parliament with a matchbox podium, bottle cap seats arranged in rows and a long banner, papers and minutes stacked everywhere.

The basement of a New York bodega seen from the floor at the eye level of a rat: towering milk crates and cases of soda and cereal boxes as high as cliffs, the warm humming glow of a refrigerator case light, a colossal orange tabby cat lying like a sphinx on a stack of crates at the far end guarding a tiny striped border gate made of coffee stirrers, a receipt roll unspooled like a road, handwritten cardboard signs, a single bare bulb.

A cavernous throne room at the bottom of a vertical porcelain shaft: far above, an open manhole shows blue sky and daylight pouring down, the base of the shaft holds a towering throne made from an upturned white porcelain toilet with a bottle cap crown above it, a colossal red rubber plunger standing like a sceptre, gold coins and lost jewelry heaped around, a ladder of rusted iron rungs climbing up toward the light, steam curling in the sunbeam.
